OLAP: Online Analytical Processing — read-optimised, multidimensional analysis of data organised as cubes of dimensions, hierarchies, and measures. OLAP trades the write performance of transactional systems for fast, intuitive slice-and-dice querying.
OLTP: Online Transaction Processing — the day-to-day operational systems (order entry, inventory) that OLAP analyses. OLTP is optimised for many small writes; OLAP for large analytical reads.
ROLAP: Relational OLAP — an architecture where the cube is not physically stored but computed on demand by translating MDX into SQL against relational star-schema tables. Mondrian is a ROLAP engine.
Mondrian: Pentaho's open-source ROLAP engine. It reads an XML schema that maps relational tables to multidimensional concepts, then translates user MDX into SQL on the fly. It powers Pentaho Analyzer.
Schema: The root XML container of a Mondrian model. It holds the logical model (cubes, shared dimensions, roles) and maps it onto the physical model (database tables). Saved as an .xml file and published to the Pentaho Server.
Cube: The analytical space for one business process — a complete set of dimensions and measures built on a fact table. Each combination of levels and measures is effectively a ready-made report.
Fact table: The central table of a star schema. It holds the numeric measures (sales, quantity) and foreign keys that join out to the dimension tables. In this course the fact table is ORDERFACT.
Dimension table: A table holding the descriptive attributes of a dimension (e.g. CUSTOMER_W_TER for customers, PRODUCTS for products), joined to the fact table by a foreign/primary key pair.
Dimension: A descriptive axis you analyse measures by — Markets, Customers, Products, Time. Dimensions are the business parameters that appear on the rows and columns of a report.
Hierarchy: An ordered set of levels within a dimension, such as Territory → Country → State → City. Each level has a one-to-many relationship with the next, giving Analyzer its drill-down and roll-up skeleton.
Level: One tier of a hierarchy, mapped to a database column (e.g. Territory → TERRITORY). Levels define the granularity at which measures aggregate.
Member: A single value within a level — for example 'EMEA' in the Territory level, or '2004' in the Years level. A set of members is what an MDX query places on an axis.
Measure: A numeric value being analysed (Sales, Quantity), defined by a fact-table column plus an aggregator and a format string. Measures roll up automatically as you drill up and down a hierarchy.
Aggregator: The function that summarises a measure across a dimension: sum, count, distinct-count, min, max, or avg. sum is the most common.
Calculated member: A measure (or member) derived from others via an MDX formula, defined once in the schema rather than recreated in each report — for example UnitPrice = [Measures].[Sales] / [Measures].[Quantity].
Named Set: A reusable, named collection of dimension members defined by an MDX expression (e.g. 'Top 3 Territories' via TopCount). Unlike a calculated member it returns a set, not a single value.
Star schema: A dimensional model with one central fact table surrounded by denormalised dimension tables — the shape OLAP prefers because it minimises joins and is easy for users to understand.
Snowflake schema: A star schema whose dimensions are normalised into multiple related tables. More storage-efficient than a star but requires more joins at query time.
Degenerate dimension: A dimension with no separate table — all its columns live in the fact table. Order Status is the classic example: few values, so a dimension table would add a join for no benefit.
Shared dimension: A dimension declared at the schema level so multiple cubes can reuse it (commonly Time). Cubes reference it with a DimensionUsage that supplies the cube-specific foreign key.
DimensionUsage: The element that references a shared dimension from inside a cube, binding it via a foreign key (e.g. <DimensionUsage name="TIME" source="TIME" foreignKey="TIME_ID"/>).
Member property: An extra attribute attached to a level (e.g. Phone, Credit Limit on Customer) for filtering and context, without adding another level to the hierarchy.
Annotation: A user-defined name/value attached to a schema element so tools can add metadata without extending Mondrian. Pentaho Analyzer reads several, such as AnalyzerDateFormat and the Geo.* roles.
AnalyzerDateFormat: An annotation on a time level (values like [yyyy] or [yyyy].['QTR'q]) that lets Pentaho Analyzer offer intelligent relative-date filters.
Geo annotations: Data.Role, Geo.Role, and Geo.RequiredParents annotations on geographic levels that tell Analyzer how to overlay results on an OpenStreetMap geo map.
Foreign key: The fact-table column that joins to a dimension (e.g. CUSTOMERNUMBER). Paired with the dimension's primary key, it tells Mondrian how to build the SQL join.
Primary key: The dimension-table column that uniquely identifies members and is referenced by the fact table's foreign key.
MDX: Multidimensional Expressions — the query language for OLAP cubes. Analyzer generates MDX as you drill and pivot; Mondrian converts it to SQL. Schema Workbench's MDX Query mode lets you write it directly.
Axis: A direction in an MDX result — typically COLUMNS and ROWS — onto which you project sets of members or measures with the SELECT clause.
Slicer: The MDX WHERE clause. It restricts the dimensional context of a query (e.g. WHERE [Markets].[APAC]) without placing the dimension on a visible axis.
TopCount: An MDX function that returns the top N members of a set ranked by a measure — e.g. TopCount([Territory].Members, 3, [Measures].[Sales]) for the three best-selling territories.
AllMembers: An MDX function (e.g. Measures.AllMembers) that returns every member of a level or dimension, including calculated ones.
SteelWheels: The fictional model-car company whose sample sales data ships with Pentaho. The SteelWheels Mondrian schema is the reference model explored in this course.
SampleData: The HSQLDB sample database (connection hsqldb_sampledata) that backs the SteelWheels schemas — it contains ORDERFACT, CUSTOMER_W_TER, PRODUCTS, DIM_TIME, and related tables.
Publish: The Schema Workbench action (File > Publish) that deploys a finished schema to the Pentaho BA Server, making it available as a data source for Analyzer reports and dashboards.
XMLA: XML for Analysis — a protocol for accessing multidimensional data. Registering a schema as an XMLA data source on publish lets external tools query the cube as if it were an Analysis Services model.
JDBC: Java Database Connectivity — the driver-based mechanism Schema Workbench uses to connect to the source database so it can read physical tables and columns when you build a schema.
Pentaho Analyzer: Pentaho's web-based OLAP analysis tool (PAZ). It queries published Mondrian cubes, letting business users slice, dice, drill, and pivot with drag-and-drop and no MDX.
Pentaho User Console: The browser-based home of the Pentaho Server (PUC, at http://localhost:8080/pentaho), where you log in to publish schemas, manage data sources, refresh caches, and create Analyzer reports.
Role: A named security identity declared in the schema with a Role element. Each role defines, through nested grants, exactly what data a user assigned to it can see in the cube.
RBAC: Role-Based Access Control — Mondrian's security model. Users are assigned roles; roles carry grants; grants filter the data each role can see.
Role mapper: The component (configured in pentahoObjects.spring.xml, bean Mondrian-UserRoleMapper) that translates Pentaho platform roles into Mondrian schema roles. Without one, Mondrian grants everyone unrestricted access.
SchemaGrant: The top-level security grant. Its access attribute (all or none) sets a role's baseline visibility of the whole schema; finer grants nest inside it.
CubeGrant: A grant nested in a SchemaGrant that allows (all) or denies (none) a role access to a specific cube. With schema access none, a CubeGrant all exposes just that cube.
HierarchyGrant: A grant that controls a role's access to a hierarchy, optionally bounded by topLevel (hide upper, aggregated levels) and bottomLevel (hide lower, detailed levels) when access is custom.
MemberGrant: The finest-grained grant — within a custom HierarchyGrant it allows or denies specific members. Order-dependent, and granting a child implicitly grants its parents.
Rollup policy: Per-hierarchy setting (full, partial, hidden) that decides how a parent total is computed when a role can see only some children — preventing users from inferring hidden values by subtraction.
Dynamic schema processor: A class implementing mondrian.spi.DynamicSchemaProcessor that filters the schema XML before Mondrian reads it. Pentaho ships one that replaces localization tokens with locale-specific text at connection time.
Tokenization: Replacing a schema's user-facing captions and descriptions with %{...} tokens (e.g. %{dimension.customers.caption}) so they can be substituted with translated text at runtime.
Locale property file: A Java MondrianMessages_<locale>.properties file mapping tokens to translated text. Mondrian's localePropFile setting points to the bundle; Java picks the file matching the user's locale.
UseContentChecksum: A data-source property that makes Mondrian expose a checksum of the schema XML so Pentaho Analyzer can detect changes and refresh its caches — required when using a dynamic schema processor.
